transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. Um... I hope it's okay that I'm here, I don't want to take up your time if it's just... well, if it's just me overreacting. 

I guess I've just been a little stressed out lately. We have a new operations manager at the plant where I work—I'm a quality inspector—and he's been sort of picking apart the inspection procedures I've used for years. I'm sure he means well and is just trying to do his job, but... I just can't seem to leave work at work anymore. 

I come home all wound up, and I feel awful about it, but I've been snapping at my husband a bit. Which really isn't like me at all. Then I just lie awake at night replaying all those meetings in my head. And the worst part is, the next day I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all. I know I shouldn't let it get to me this much, and I'm trying to handle it better... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you might be able to help me with?
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I still really love being with my husband, and I still look forward to my weekend gardening. I mean, I really try hard to keep up with all of that. I definitely haven't lost interest in my family or anything. 

Even though I've been a bit irritable, like I mentioned before, I still want to be around them and do our normal things. I'm really trying my best not to let the work stress ruin our time together at home. Does that help answer your question? I hope it's a good sign that I still care about all of those things.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things other than work, like your health, family, or everyday responsibilities, even when there isn’t a clear problem?

No, not really. I mean, I try not to be a worrier in general. I think I handle everyday things pretty well, and my health is fine. My family is doing well, too. It's really just this situation at the plant that's got me all tied up in knots. I hope that's okay to say... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I really don't think I worry too much about anything else, just the work stuff right now.
Do you find it hard to control your worry about work, even when you try to focus on something else?

Um, well... I try really hard to focus on other things, I promise I do. When I'm gardening or watching TV with my husband, I make a real effort to just be in the moment. 

But sometimes... well, sometimes it's like my brain just keeps looping back to what the manager said about my last report, even when I'm trying not to think about it. I can usually push it away eventually, though! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing all day. I do manage to get it under control most of the time... is that normal? I mean, I hope it doesn't sound like I'm not trying hard enough to let it go.
Have you noticed any changes in your body because of the stress, like feeling restless, tense muscles, trouble sleeping, or getting tired more easily than usual?

Um, no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I sleep pretty well, honestly. I always try to make sure I get a good night's rest so I'm ready for my shift. 

I'm on my feet a lot doing inspections at the plant, so sure, sometimes I'm a little tired at the end of the day, but just... normal tired, you know? Not because of the stress. My muscles feel fine, and I definitely don't feel restless or anything. I really try to take good care of myself physically. 

I hope it's a good thing that I don't have any of those issues to report? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right and giving you what you need. But yeah, physically, I promise I'm holding up just fine.
Would you say that your worry about work feels persistent or hard to control, even when you're not actively thinking about it?

Um, well, like I was saying before... I really do try my best to keep it under control. I don't want to sound like I'm just letting it take over, because I'm not. 

I guess... sometimes it does kind of sit in the back of my mind, even when I'm not actively trying to figure out what to do about the plant. But I wouldn't say it's completely out of my control, you know? I can usually snap myself out of it if I just focus really hard on whatever I'm doing, like my gardening. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm not handling things well. I'm really trying to be positive about it all. Is it okay that it still pops up sometimes, even when I'm trying to be good and not dwell on it?
Has this stress about work made it harder for you to function in any important areas of your life, like your job performance, relationships, or daily routines?

Um... well, I really try not to let it affect things too much, I promise. I always want to do a good job. But, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, things have slipped just a little bit lately. 

I've missed a couple of internal deadlines at the plant, which isn't like me at all. And I haven't been going to some of the meetings I'm supposed to be at... I just kind of pull back from them right now. I hope you don't think I'm a bad employee, I really am trying to get back on track with all of that.

And at home... well, my husband and I have been bickering a little more than usual. Nothing terrible! Just... arguing a bit more. And I haven't been keeping up with our normal evening routines, like making dinner or tidying up, quite the way I used to. 

I feel awful even admitting that, because I pride myself on keeping a nice home and being a good wife. Is it normal for things to slide a little bit when you're under this much pressure? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, but I really am trying my best to fix it all.
Have you been feeling down or blaming yourself more than usual, even when things aren’t your fault?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely try to keep a positive attitude about things. I don't think I've been feeling particularly down, or at least, I try not to let myself get that way. 

And as for blaming myself... well, I know the issues at the plant aren't entirely my fault, so I try not to take it all on my shoulders. I mean, maybe I'm a little hard on myself sometimes because I just want everything to go smoothly, but I wouldn't say I'm blaming myself for things I didn't do. 

I hope that's the right answer? I really just try to stay focused on doing my job the best I can and not let myself get bogged down in negative thoughts. Is it okay that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you felt down, sad, or hopeless for most of the day, more days than not, even if just a little bit?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to keep my spirits up as much as I can. I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless... definitely not most of the day or anything like that. 

I mean, sure, everyone has moments where they feel a little overwhelmed, right? But I always try to look on the bright side and just keep pushing forward. I don't want to be one of those people who just gives up or sits around feeling sorry for themselves. 

So, no, I don't think I've been feeling hopeless. I'm still trying my hardest to make things work. I hope that's a good thing? I just really want to show that I'm trying to stay strong through all of this.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge for more days than not, even if just a little bit, and does it feel hard to control that anxiety even when you try?

Um... anxious? Well, I guess maybe a little bit, but nothing I can't handle, I promise. I try really hard not to be an anxious person. 

I mean, with the new quality control standards at the plant, I do feel a little... keyed up sometimes? Just because I want to make sure I'm doing everything exactly right. But I wouldn't say I'm on edge most days. And I definitely try to keep it under control. I do my deep breathing and just tell myself to focus on the task in front of me. 

I'm really trying not to let the stress get the better of me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as someone who just falls apart under pressure, because I really do try to keep it together.
Have you felt nervous, anxious, or on edge about things other than work, even a little bit, over the past few weeks?

Um... no, not really. Outside of work, I think I'm doing pretty well. I mean, work is definitely the main thing on my mind right now, with all the changes and everything. 

But at home, or just in general? No, I wouldn't say I'm nervous or on edge. I try to leave the work stress at the plant, you know? When I'm off the clock, I just try to relax and focus on normal things. I don't want to be one of those people who brings all their baggage home and worries about every little thing in life. 

So, I think I'm keeping it pretty balanced outside of the job. Is that what you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm handling things.
Have you found yourself worrying about things other than work, like social situations, minor everyday matters, or future events, even when there’s no clear reason to be concerned?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try not to fret over little everyday things or... or what might happen in the future. I mean, there's no sense in getting all worked up when there's no real reason to, right? 

I think I do a pretty good job of just letting normal, everyday stuff roll off my back. I just go about my day, run my errands, and try to be pleasant. I really want to be the kind of person who handles life gracefully, you know? I'm definitely not a worrier by nature. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm answering everything the way you need me to.
Would you say that your anxiety about work feels excessive or more intense than the situation actually warrants, even when you try to calm yourself down?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's excessive. Um... I really think it's just the normal amount of concern for the situation. Because, you know, as an inspector, my whole job is to catch mistakes, and with the new plant standards... well, it actually warrants a little bit of extra focus right now. 

I definitely don't let it get out of hand or blow things out of proportion. I'm very careful about that. I just want to do a good job and be responsible. I hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable? I just try to be really conscientious about my work, and I think I keep it pretty well in check.
Have you found it harder to concentrate on tasks at work or home because your mind is preoccupied with work-related worries?

Oh, no... no, I don't think so. I really pride myself on being very attentive. In my line of work, you know, as an inspector, you absolutely have to stay focused, so I always make sure that I am. Even if I have a lot on my mind with all the new plant standards, I don't let it distract me from the actual task right in front of me. 

I would hate for anyone to think I'm slipping or not doing my job properly, so I push through it. And at home... well, I just get my chores done like always. I try very hard to stay on top of everything and not let my mind wander. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right answers and being helpful.
Even though you try to manage your anxiety about work, would you say it causes you a lot of distress or makes it hard for you to do the things you need to do during the day?

Oh... um... well, I wouldn't say a *lot* of distress. I really do try to keep a brave face and handle things. 

But... I guess if I have to be completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information—my work record might have taken a little bit of a hit recently. It's actually really embarrassing to admit, especially after I just said how focused I try to be, but... I've missed a few internal deadlines lately. And I sort of... pulled back from some meetings I'm expected to attend. I just didn't want anyone to see me flustered, you know? I didn't want to bring the team down. 

And at home, it's... well, my husband and I are arguing a bit more than normal. I just haven't been keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I always used to, and I feel just awful about it. I'm really trying to fix it and get back to normal, I promise. I hope you don't think too badly of me for letting things slip a little? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.

The patient's symptom profile for Adjustment Disorder does not include a specific symptom regarding the anxiety being 'excessive' or 'more intense than the situation warrants' (in fact, in Adjustment Disorder the distress is out of proportion, but the provided profiles only have Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response, Additional Requirements 1 & 2, Functional Impairment, and Duration). None of the available keys directly match the concept of anxiety being excessive compared to what the situation warrants, although the maladaptive response is related. However, since the question is specifically probing for GAD criterion (excessive worry/anxiety out of proportion), and the profile lacks a specific GAD excessive worry symptom, it maps to None.

patient.answer:
Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's excessive. Um... I really think it's just the normal amount of concern for the situation. Because, you know, as an inspector, my whole job is to catch mistakes, and with the new plant standards... well, it actually warrants a little bit of extra focus right now. 

I definitely don't let it get out of hand or blow things out of proportion. I'm very careful about that. I just want to do a good job and be responsible. I hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable? I just try to be really conscientious about my work, and I think I keep it pretty well in check.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant difficulty concentrating due to work-related stress, which would help distinguish between adjustment disorder with anxiety (F43.22) and generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1).
doctor.question: Have you found it harder to concentrate on tasks at work or home because your mind is preoccupied with work-related worries?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about difficulty concentrating as a symptom of anxiety (often associated with GAD or generalized anxiety). My symptom profile covers functional impairment (missing deadlines, pulling back from meetings, arguing at home), but it does not specifically include a manifestation about difficulty concentrating due to being preoccupied with worries.

patient.answer:
Oh, no... no, I don't think so. I really pride myself on being very attentive. In my line of work, you know, as an inspector, you absolutely have to stay focused, so I always make sure that I am. Even if I have a lot on my mind with all the new plant standards, I don't let it distract me from the actual task right in front of me. 

I would hate for anyone to think I'm slipping or not doing my job properly, so I push through it. And at home... well, I just get my chores done like always. I try very hard to stay on top of everything and not let my mind wander. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right answers and being helpful.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment specifically due to difficulty controlling anxiety about work, even though they are trying to manage it.
doctor.question: Even though you try to manage your anxiety about work, would you say it causes you a lot of distress or makes it hard for you to do the things you need to do during the day?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My work record has taken a hit because I’ve missed internal deadlines and pulled back from meetings I’m expected to attend. At home, my husband and I are arguing more, and I’m not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the anxiety causes distress or makes it hard to do things during the day, which directly assesses functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Oh... um... well, I wouldn't say a *lot* of distress. I really do try to keep a brave face and handle things. 

But... I guess if I have to be completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information—my work record might have taken a little bit of a hit recently. It's actually really embarrassing to admit, especially after I just said how focused I try to be, but... I've missed a few internal deadlines lately. And I sort of... pulled back from some meetings I'm expected to attend. I just didn't want anyone to see me flustered, you know? I didn't want to bring the team down. 

And at home, it's... well, my husband and I are arguing a bit more than normal. I just haven't been keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I always used to, and I feel just awful about it. I'm really trying to fix it and get back to normal, I promise. I hope you don't think too badly of me for letting things slip a little? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a prolonged stress reaction specifically tied to a psychosocial stressor at work, leading to mild functional impairment in both occupational and interpersonal domains. The symptoms are not excessive or pervasive enough to meet criteria for generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1), as the anxiety is circumscribed to work-related concerns and does not generalize to other areas of life. The pattern is consistent with adjustment disorder with anxiety (F43.22), with a clear temporal relationship to a psychosocial stressor (new manager and changes in work procedures).
